question: Which scientist thought of the concept of steady state of the universe?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fred Hoyle.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fred Hoyle:-**

 
 
• He​** **is the **scientist **who thought of the concept of the **steady state of the universe.**
 
• Steady state theory suggests that the universe has **no beginning or end** and that new matter is continuously created to **maintain a constant density.**
 
• Hoyle proposed this theory as an **alternative to the Big Bang theory**, which suggests that the universe began with a massive explosion.
 
• Hoyle's theory was** widely debated and eventually fell out **of favor as evidence for the Big Bang theory mounted.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Edwin Hubble:-**

 
 
• He is known for his work on the** expanding universe** and the** discovery of galaxies** beyond the Milky Way.
 
 
 
• **Harold Jeffrey:-**
 
 
• He was an **American mathematician **who worked on the theory of **partial differential equations and geophysics.**
 
 
 
• **Pierre-Simon Laplace:-**
 
 
• He was a **French mathematician** and** astronomer** who made significant contributions to celestial mechanics and statistics.
